chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from 'Ali ibn Mahziyar from Hammad ibn 'Isa from Hariz ibn 'Abdillah from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is sufficient of the words in the Tashahhud in the first two rak'ahs?' He said, 'You say: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner.' I said: 'And what is sufficient of the Tashahhud for the last two rak'ahs?' He said, 'The two testimonies (al-Shahadatayn).'

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: Tashahhud, the sitting testimony in prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the specific words to recite in the Tashahhud during the first and last two rak'ahs of prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the abbreviated testimony in the first two rak'ahs and the full Shahada required in the final two, reflecting the Imami practice of brevity in the initial sitting. It underscores the theological centrality of Tawhid (monotheism) and the Prophetic mission within the daily ritual, linking the physical act of prayer to the core declaration of faith. This specific formulation highlights the scholarly emphasis on precise verbal adherence to the Imams' instructions for valid worship.
